rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so the safe move is to raise obfuscation intensity across the board rather than retune defensively. This is a tiny C++ program (34 functions, ~3.6 KB text) dominated by small Tree constructors and a modest main, so absolute size growth from BCF/FLA is cheap in bytes while flattening and bogus control flow in these small, branch-light functions yield disproportionate RE resistance; accordingly FLA SizeCost and BCF SecurityGain were raised so they apply more broadly alongside SUB. SUB gets the strongest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since arithmetic substitution is near-free on this simple code. ICALL and IGV are pushed harder (0.85) because indirect dispatch and global-to-local variable remapping disrupt the structural signatures of the repeated constructor pairs (C1/C2 duplicates) and string-heavy Tree setup, which are the easiest anchors for a reverser; their CorrectnessRisk weights stay moderate at 0.25 to permit application while the clean round-1 run suggests vtable/constructor interactions are tolerable. SPLIT stays the lightest pass (0.60) since its blocks are already tiny and it mainly serves as a diversity multiplier for FLA/BCF rather than a primary defense. Runtime weights were kept in the 0.45-0.60 band overall: acceptable per-function growth without letting the scheduler reject the hotspot main on cost grounds.
